title: An evaluation of the implementation of a cross-indication case management within the medical rehabilitation services of the German Pension Insurance of Central Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung Mitteldeutschland)
summary: Some rehabilitation patients need support after medical rehabilitation to get a job or use existing social support services. To help with this, the Pension Insurance of Central Germany (Deutsche Rentenversicherung Mitteldeutschland (DRV MD)) has introduced cross-indication case management (FM). This is done by the vocational training centres (BFW) in Central Germany with the medical rehabilitation facilities. The BEiFall project is monitoring and evaluating this process. The primary goals are to evaluate the cross-indication implementation phase and to identify ways to improve it. A mixed-methods design is used to examine the experiences of rehabilitation patients, the support they receive and the challenges they face. We will also interview rehabilitation patients with and without FM, as well as FM managers in the rehabilitation centres and BFWs. Rehabilitation patients are also asked about their support needs at two points in time: at the end of their medical rehabilitation (t0) and 9 months after medical rehabilitation (t1). A questionnaire is also given to DRV MD rehabilitation patients at the same times as the FM-group. A routine data analysis is being prepared on the social and medical progress of all DRV MD rehabilitation patients, based on routine data of the DRV MD.

interventions.name: At the interface of rehabilitation aftercare, prescribed case management (FM) is intended to ensure continuous supportive assistance with reintegration into working life, based on the individual's life situation and personal needs.
